text: The case facts and route history, the balance and asset state, the document index and registration, the pack run and the WO package are consumed on their owners' published contracts, never as tables or views, and their operation names stay placeholders until the owners publish them.
why: Only rwb-source-data holds SELECT on the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views, only rwb-case writes recovery_case and only rwb-document writes document, while rwb-decision governs the rule rows and rwb-agent runs the pack. TSD S7 T5.2 names the published interfaces only as module interfaces and publishes no operation name, so no name may be invented, and DP-05 moves the legacy v_ace_account and v_ace_npa_asset reads onto the owner's data product with no v_ace_* grant here. The plan's C row for the slice is empty, so the seven rows are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata.
read: FSD S7 A2.3.2 and A2.3.3.1; TSD S7 T5.2 and T-A.1; context pack ownership rows and connection-matrix row S7; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-05
applied_in: RWB-S7-E6015-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 10, 11 and 12.2; RWB-S7-E6015-CON sections 2, 3, 7 AC3, 11 and 12.2
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-document and rwb-decision, before the contract is tagged
impact: The app story builds on Day 1 against seven contract fakes with a 2 s budget and a breaker, and a statement on a v_ace_* view, a recovery_case row or a document row fails the boundary test

text: The WO rule package is read as data at its version in force from rwb-decision and evaluated by this service's own evaluator inside the pack activity; no embedded Drools kit row is added to the metadata, so RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and RWB-P7-E1073-CON are recorded as absent.
why: DP-04 is not in the pattern set the plan gives this key, yet the step evaluates R-WO-05 of a route set of 51 rules over 27 states and ADR-017 keeps the rule models in rwb-decision and the evaluation in the owning service. The connection matrix also gives S7 one Temporal call to P7 that no source ties to a named operation. Keeping the plan's H row unchanged and recording the kit as a tracked dependency is the only choice that does not invent a metadata value.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04 and R5.4 class H; TSD S7 T2 and T4; context pack Temporal and Drools slides 12 and 13 and connection-matrix row S7; split plan H list
applied_in: RWB-S7-E6015-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 8 BR7, 12.2, 12.5 and 13; RWB-S7-E6015-CON sections 2, 3, 8 BR10 and 13
confirm: Solution architect and the rule owner in rwb-decision, before wave 4 starts
impact: The package arrives on its read with the version recorded with each outcome, no kit is embedded, and the matrix's Temporal call to P7 stays a recorded gap

text: The pack is assembled by the write-off agent run of rwb-agent, consumed as a contract row under a service identity; the dependency is recorded although DP-20 is not in the pattern set and the connection-matrix cell S7 to P10 is empty.
why: R-WO-05 reads 'Write-off agent prepares the pack', its Systems column names the Agent Runtime, FSD S7 A2.3.2 names the Workbench document hub beside it and legacy AC2 says the write-off agent prepares the pack. The pack cannot be assembled without that run, so the row is consumed on the owner's contract; adding C RWB-P10-TE013-CON to the metadata would invent a dependency the plan does not hold, so it is tracked instead.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-WO-05; FSD S7 A2.3.2; legacy RWB-E6-015 AC2; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-20; context pack connection-matrix row S7 (column P10 empty)
applied_in: RWB-S7-E6015-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 12.2, 12.5 and 13; RWB-S7-E6015-CON sections 2, 3, 7 AC3, 8 BR6 and 12.2
confirm: Solution architect and the owner of rwb-agent, before the contract is tagged
impact: The pack content comes from the agent on its contract with a fake on Day 1, and the missing pattern row and matrix cell are in the registers for the plan owner

text: The pack document is registered in rwb-document and its reference is carried in the pack element; the provision carried, the residual and the pack document reference have no column in write_off and are not copied into the row.
why: R-WO-05 names the provision carried and the residual, R-WO-09 tests provision_carried and pack_document_id and legacy AC2 lists the residual, yet TSD S7 T3.1 gives no such field on write_off and the legacy Data table names document as a P5 table. Inventing a column would break DP-15 and the per-service migration rule, so the three elements live in the pack element and the row carries the amount.
read: TSD S7 T3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-WO-05 and R-WO-09; legacy RWB-E6-015 Data; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-15
applied_in: RWB-S7-E6015-APP sections 2, 4, 11, 12.7 and 13; RWB-S7-E6015-CON sections 2, 7 AC2, 11 and 12.7
confirm: Solution architect and the data steward, before the contract is tagged
impact: No migration is written by this story, and a column for any of the three is a DB change of this service to be raised by the plan owner

text: The pack step writes the write_off row of the case and reads tax_criteria_met, which the tax criteria step wrote; the amount written off is the balance the pack carries.
why: No source names the step that inserts the write_off row, and both E6-013 and E6-014 could carry it. The pack step is the first step that needs the whole row, it must write the row inside the transaction of its decision record, and tax_criteria_met is the recorded result of FEAT-WOF-02, so the pack reads it rather than computing it again. FSD S7 A2.3.3.1 gives VR-S7-003-1 to this feature and the tax criteria version is therefore read here.
read: TSD S7 T3.1 and T2; FSD S7 A2.3.3.1 and A2.2; legacy RWB-E6-015 Data and AC2
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of RWB-S7-E6013-APP and RWB-S7-E6014-APP, before the row writer is built
impact: One row is written once per case, the tax criteria result is not recomputed, and a version conflict between the two stories is settled before wave 4 starts

text: The pack step publishes no event: the service's event EV-24, which TSD S7 T5.3 names WriteOffApproved, is the committee approval's and DP-09 is recorded as an absent library row.
why: No source ties EV-24 to the name WriteOffApproved or to the pack step, and the pack approves nothing, so it cannot publish an approval event. DP-09 is not in the pattern set of this key although the service owns a topic, so the outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is recorded as an absent H row rather than added to the metadata.

impact: No producer group, no outbox row and no event name are declared by this story, and the identity of EV-24 is confirmed by the committee story

text: SCR-27 reads the pack through the gateway-bff composite route, and the write-off read the route needs is not in the Ownership Map, so it carries a placeholder and is declared as an edge and platform item rather than a path of this story.
why: The screen must show the pack of a case, the Ownership Map gives rwb-writeoff exactly two operations, POST /write-off-scans and POST /write-offs/{writeOffId}/committee-decision, and neither reads a write_off row. Inventing a GET path would contradict the Ownership Map, which is the authority for operations, so the read is recorded as a gap for the map owner and the screen field list is left to RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

confirm: Solution architect and the Ownership Map owner, before SCR-27 is built
impact: The screen is served by the composite route with a placeholder read until the map is corrected, and no operation is claimed by this legacy key

text: The recovery history of the pack is the route history and the case facts read on the rwb-case contract; no payment or proceeds row is named for the pack and none is read.
why: Legacy AC1 and the feature text name the recovery history, the legacy Data table carries no payment or proceeds entity, and rwb-payment is reached by S7 only through Temporal and events in the post charge-off steps (context pack connection matrix, row S7). Reading payment facts in the pack step would need a dependency no source gives, so the history is the case-side one and the rest is recorded.
read: Legacy RWB-E6-015 AC1 and Data; FSD S7 A2.3.1 and A2.3.2; context pack connection-matrix row S7
confirm: Business lead of S7 and the solution architect, before wave 4 starts
impact: The pack carries the case-side history and no payment read, and a richer history is a change request on the rwb-payment contract
